messages.subject: Re: How can I get install_github to keep the source?
messages.subject_clean: How can I get install_github to keep the source?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Alastair,

This is a bit confusing - in this context, keeping the source means
that when you inspect an R function from the console you can see the
original source (including comments etc).  You still won't be able to
see the source code as source files inside the R directory of the
installed package.

Hadley

On Tue, Jul 24, 2012 at 5:52 AM, Alastair Andrew
<alastai...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi,
>
> I've been trying to install yihui's knitr package from github and retain the
> source so I can edit some of the tikz handling functions. I'm using the v
> 0.7.1 of the devtools library on R 2.15.1 running on Mac OS X 10.6.8.
> According to the 0.7 release notes (and the discussion relating to issue #90
> on the github repo) the default behaviour of install is to retain the
> source, but whenever I look in my R Framework's knitr/R directory all I see
> are the knitr, knitr.rdb and knitr.rdx. Does install_github not use the same
> defaults as install?
>
> I've tried running:
> library(devtools)
> install_github("knitr", "yihui")
> install_github("knitr", "yihui", args = c("--with-keep.source"))
>
> Am I using this function correctly? Is the expected behaviour that
> install_github won't keep the source? I would have thought that passing the
> explicit args parameter would work.
>
> Any help would be appreciated.
> Cheers,
> Alastair
>

--
Assistant Professor / Dobelman Family Junior Chair
Department of Statistics / Rice University
http://had.co.nz/

messages.body_plain:
Thanks Hadley,

I'd interpreted --with-keep.source to mean I'd have access to all the .R files that I can see in yihui's github repo. There's a particular function (save_plot) I want to edit to try and add support for lualatex. I know where the function is within his plot.R file. If I install knitr with the source should I'd expect to be able to do:

library(devtools)
install_github("knitr", "yihui")

library(knitr)
body(save_plot)
# or
trace(save_plot, edit = TRUE)

like for other libraries to see the function code from within an R session? Neither of these approaches seem to work. I am missing something subtle about R's package or namespace system.

Apologies in advance if you feel this is drifting off-topic from a specific devtools question into more general R package development.
Thanks,
Alastair

messages.subject: Re: How can I get install_github to keep the source?
messages.subject_clean: How can I get install_github to keep the source?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Alastair,

If you're trying to modify a function in knitr, you'd be better off
downloading the complete source (or better, forking and cloning), then
modifying the files on disk and use load_all("path/to/knitr") to
reload and test.  Yihui might also have other suggestions for
contributing to knitr, so I've also cc'd him.

This mailing list is also for general package development questions :)

Hadley
